body.statement:
A single nonrefinable dyadic interval for a public control does not suffice for a quantile enclosure whose required width tends to zero.  Suppose instead that every public control is an exact dyadic input.  Put
\[
h_\alpha=\lceil\log_2(64/\alpha)\rceil,
\qquad
g_n=20\{h_\alpha+\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil+1\},
\]
\[
p_n=n^2+4g_n,\qquad q_n=p_n-g_n,\qquad
\tau_n=B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1,
\]
and define the exactly comparable dyadic upper bound
\[
\overline\tau_n=B+\sigma\{12(n+1)+1\}+1\ge\tau_n.
\]
For a sufficiently large fixed integer \(C_\star\), put
\[
L_n=p_n+\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil
+\lceil\log_2\overline\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star.
\]
Then these schedules are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge\tau_n\), and the composed measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) satisfies
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1}),
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]\over w_n}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
{\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]\over w_n}
\le K_\alpha.
\]
On \(\kappa_n=0\),
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}};
\]
on \(\kappa_n=1\), \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}=[-M_0,M_0]\).  Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\),
\[
{\varepsilon_n\over a_n}\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability},
\qquad
{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\over2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\]
Finally, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), the expectation of every nonnegative recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) is \(o(n^{-1})\).  In particular, this holds along every sequence with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\).  A polynomial-time extension to refinable non-dyadic controls requires schedules parameterized by an explicit uniform time-and-output-size modulus.
body.proof_tex:
For \(x\ge0\), \(\sqrt x\le x+1\), and \(\log(e+n)\le n+1\); hence the displayed exact dyadic \(\overline\tau_n\) is at least \(\tau_n\).  The schedule and \(\textnormal{def:observation-encoding}\) give
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}
=2^{L_n-p_n-\lceil\log_2(p_n+2)\rceil-4}
=2^{\lceil\log_2\overline\tau_n\rceil+2g_n+C_\star-4}
\ge\overline\tau_n\ge\tau_n
\tag{1}
\]
when \(C_\star\ge4\).  The schedules \(p_n,q_n,L_n\), and the binary encoding length \(\lceil\log_2T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\rceil\), are polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\); numerically, \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) is bounded by a fixed power of \((n+2)/\alpha\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(L_n\) also dominates the fixed encoding lengths of the exact-dyadic public controls.  A rounded observation coordinate has numerator length at most
\[
p_n+\lceil\log_2(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+1)\rceil+2
\tag{2}
\]
and exponent-description length \(O(\log(p_n+2))\); a sufficiently large fixed \(C_\star\) therefore places every encoded input in \(\mathbb D_{L_n}\).

There are \(N_n=n^2+2n\le3n^2\) observed coordinates, each with mean bounded by \(B\).  For \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), exponential Markov inequalities give
\[
P(|Z|>x)\le2e^{-x^2/2},\qquad x\ge0.
\tag{3}
\]
By (1), a union bound yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P_P(\kappa_n=1)
\le2N_ne^{-6\log(e+n)}
\le6n^2(e+n)^{-6}=O(n^{-4})=o(n^{-1}).
\tag{4}
\]

We next control the only event on which the sharp numerical bound can fail.  Let \(\mathcal N\) be a \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere with \(|\mathcal N|\le9^n\), obtained by the disjoint-ball volume comparison.  Approximation in both arguments gives
\[
\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{x,y\in\mathcal N}|x^{\top}Ey|.
\tag{5}
\]
Each \(x^{\top}Ey/\sigma\) is standard normal.  Equations (3)--(5) imply constants \(k_0>0\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(c,\sigma\), for which
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P_P\{\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}>cn/8\}
\le2\,9^{2n}\exp\left(-{c^2n^2\over512\sigma^2}\right)
\le e^{-k_0n^2}
\tag{6}
\]
for \(n\ge n_0\).  The min--max formula gives
\[
|s_j(A+E)-s_j(A)|\le\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{7}
\]
On the complement of (6), exact rank and strong spectrum imply
\[
s_r(X)\ge7cn/8,\qquad s_{r+1}(X)\le cn/8,\qquad
s_1(X)\le C_0n+cn/8.
\tag{8}
\]
The true donor and any matrix in its encoding box differ entrywise by at most \(2^{-p_n}\), hence in operator norm by at most \(n2^{-p_n}\).  Since \(c\le1\) and \(C_0\ge2\), equations (8) imply, for all sufficiently large \(n\), that every matrix in the box satisfies
\[
s_r\ge3cn/4,\qquad s_{r+1}\le cn/4,\qquad
s_1\le3C_0n/2.
\tag{9}
\]

Put
\[
H_n=n+T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\alpha^{-1}+p_n+q_n+1.
\tag{10}
\]
The schedules make \(H_n\) a polynomial in \(n\) for fixed \(\alpha\).  The proposed and proved \(\textnormal{lem:stable-certified-padding}\), together with (6)--(9), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[&(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=0\}] 
&\le K H_n^k(2^{-p_n}+2^{1-q_n})+K H_n^k e^{-k_0n^2}
=o(n^{-m})
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
for every fixed \(m>0\), because \(p_n=n^2+O(\log n)\) and \(q_n=n^2+O(\log n)\).  Every recorded radius is nonnegative and bounded by their sum, so (11) holds for each summand separately.  This also verifies the early-kill requirement uniformly for loading norms from zero through their \(B\sqrt n\) bound: the numerical estimate (11) does not divide by a loading.

The corrected \(\textnormal{thm:deterministic-dyadic-certificate}\) applies because all public controls are exact dyadics.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), it gives
\[
I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_n
\le2(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}+\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}})
=2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}.
\tag{12}
\]
On \(\kappa_n=1\), the composed procedure returns \([-M_0,M_0]\).  This contains the target because
\[
|\theta_n|
\le\|u\|_2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|v\|_2
\le(B\sqrt n){1\over cn}(B\sqrt n)=M_0.
\tag{13}
\]
Also \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2M_0\) on that branch.  Equations (4), (11)--(13) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]=o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[M_0\mathbf1\{\kappa_n=1\}]=o(n^{-1}),
\tag{14}
\]
as well as every summand-by-summand assertion.

Pointwise, (12)--(13) show that coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) entails coverage by \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\).  The proved \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-coverage}\) therefore gives the first limit.  Furthermore,
\[
w_n\ge b_n=\sigma^2\|A^+\|_{\mathrm F}
\ge{\sigma^2\over s_1(A)}\ge{\sigma^2\over C_0n}.
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (14)--(15),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}{\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]\over w_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Since \(x\le y+[x-y]_+\) for nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})
\le\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})+\varepsilon_n.
\tag{17}
\]
The established \(\textnormal{thm:transition-length}\) and (16) give the asserted transition-order expected length.

If \(b_n/a_n\to0\), equation (15) implies
\[
na_n\ge{\sigma^2\over C_0}{a_n\over b_n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{18}
\]
By (14),
\[
{\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]\over a_n}
={n\mathbb E_{P_n}[\varepsilon_n]\over na_n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) in \(L^1(P_n)\) and in probability.  On \(\kappa_n=0\), (12) makes the length difference nonnegative and at most \(\varepsilon_n\); the exceptional probability tends to zero by (4).  Therefore
\[
{\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})-
\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{out}})\over a_n}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\tag{20}
\]
The proved \(\textnormal{thm:oracle-length}\) and (20) establish the Gaussian length ratio.  Equations (11) and (14) are uniform over the entire class, so they imply the final rank-one joint-zero assertion as a special case.

Finally, suppose only one fixed dyadic interval of positive width is supplied for a public control that enters a strictly monotone quantile.  Two distinct control values in that interval induce two distinct quantiles.  An algorithm receiving the same fixed interval under both values cannot return enclosures of both with widths tending to zero.  Thus a nonrefinable interval is insufficient.  A refinement oracle avoids this indistinguishability only when its uniform production modulus is included in the schedules, exactly as stated.
body.justification: Explicit polynomial schedules transfer the deterministic certificate back to the original continuous Gaussian observations while making every numerical-padding component negligible at the \(n^{-1}\) transition floor.
body.gap: The result is a certified arithmetic theorem rather than verified source code and assumes exact-dyadic public controls.
body.consumer: CAST-style software can preserve the paper's coverage and oracle-length guarantees when it implements the stated outward certificate and encoding interface.
